messages:
elaine: quick sync — we're running bring-up for Novus-Mini v2.7B. License snippet: 'Non-Commercial use only; Model weights and modified binaries may not be redistributed for commercial purposes; Attribution must be displayed where model outputs are shown.' Questions: (1) can Dedicated customers get quantized files? (2) can we serve embeddings to paying customers if model runs on our infra? (3) what exact attribution wording/placement suffices?
jamal (legal): initial read: NC + no-redistribution = blocks commercial hosting and handing out quantized binaries. Need to see full license. If it's explicit NC, hosting paid inference == commercial use -> likely prohibited. Share the upstream link?
mika: infra perspective: if we never hand over a quantized artifact and only run the model in our runtime, that feels like "use" not redistribution. But NC terms can still prohibit commercial use. Also some licenses treat in-memory transformed weights as derivatives. Risky.
elaine: link: https://example.org/novus-mini/LICENSE. Exact clause: "Model weights and modified binaries may not be redistributed for commercial purposes. Attribution must be displayed where model outputs are shown."
jamal (legal): thanks. Given that clause: - Hosted API to paying customers = commercial -> disallowed. - Shipping quantized weights to Dedicated customers = redistribution of binaries -> disallowed. - Private/BYOW where customer provides original weights and we only orchestrate = generally okay, but require customer attestation that they hold commercial rights. We'll loop in compliance.
tom-infra: operationally we can implement BYOW onboarding flow with an explicit attestation and a hash check of provided weights. That keeps us from redistributing artifacts. We should add a blocked-features flag for Hosted that prevents enabling Novus-Mini endpoints by default.
mika: embeddings question: license targets weights/binaries, but it also requires attribution on outputs. Even if embeddings aren't called out, the license's spirit is to restrict commercial exploitation. I'd advise to treat embeddings as disallowed for paid customers until legal signs off.
jamal (legal): agree. Conservative approach: no commercial serving of outputs unless upstream grants a commercial license or clarifies permitted uses. For attribution: the license says outputs must display attribution. We should show: 'Powered by Novus-Mini v2.7B — License: https://example.org/novus-mini/LICENSE' near any UI that displays model outputs and include the same string in developer-facing docs/response headers for API customers. I'll draft a short template.
elaine: small tech nuance: what about ephemeral quantization at runtime (no file persisted)? Does that change the analysis?
jamal (legal): ambiguous. Some licensors argue any transformed form is a derivative. Don't rely on that as a compliance strategy for commercial hosting.
tom-infra: action items: add feature-flag to block Novus-Mini on Hosted; extend BYOW onboarding with the attestation + compliance ticket template; add an internal note to pause commercial eval benchmarks.
mika: we'll pause the commercial eval suite and mark the model as "research-only" in the model catalog until legal confirms.
jamal (legal): recommend to product/customers: (A) request a commercial license from upstream; (B) ask for a redistribution carve-out for quantized weights; or (C) only permit BYOW private deployments and internal research. For educational/nonprofit customers we can consider hosted access with a signed non-commercial attestation, but needs compliance approval. I'll produce a concise guidance blurb (allowed/disallowed use list + attribution template + BYOW attestation) by EOD.
opsbot: tag added: #legal-triage :white_check_mark:
elaine: thanks — tagging product leads so Hosted rollout is blocked until we have a commercial license or an explicit exception. I'll update the onboarding checklist once jamal posts the blurb.
